model.name: Software Product
model.purpose: Describe a software product in full operating context: the offered identity and producer roles, published releases and channels, integrity and provenance of distributable artifacts, the product-level bill of materials and declared dependencies, support and end-of-life state, security advisories and exploitability assertions, and the deployed systems and environments where a release actually runs.
model.scope_statement: This standalone meta-model covers software as a double-lived subject: a published offering with versions, licenses-as-references, and composition evidence, and an operated installation with inventory tags, environments and exposure. Semantics are format-neutral. SPDX, CycloneDX, SWID/CoSWID, CSAF, PURL and CPE are alignments and interchange projections, not the model. Fine-grained component and package internals belong to WM-SFT-007 via COMPOSE. Legal license instruments, organization master data, identifier-scheme registries and datasets are sibling references, not local masters.
in_scope: Software product identity, aliases, family, edition, SKU and persistent product line identifiers
Producer, creator, supplier, maintainer, distributor, licensor and tag-creator roles as references to an organization model
Release version strings, version schemes, channels, pre-release and colloquial versions
Publication, withdrawal, yank, supersession, patch versus upgrade, and tag-revision without a software-version change
Integrity hashes, signatures and content identifiers of release artifacts and of SBOM or advisory documents
Product- and release-grain Software Bills of Materials, SBOM types and generation context
Declared dependency edges, version constraints, scope and resolution to a release, with component nodes composed from WM-SFT-007
Completeness, coverage, known unknowns and composition aggregate status
Support level, valid-until time, end of support, end of life and disposal of the software product or release line
Security advisories, VEX product status, remediations and advisory tracking
Deployed system records, endpoint tag lifecycle (corpus, primary, patch, supplemental), hosting environment and discovery evidence
Delivery mode classification including application, library, container, firmware-as-software, and SaaS/service offerings at product grain
Disclosure, TLP and sharing constraints for catalogues, SBOMs and inventories
out_of_scope: Internal structure, files, snippets and package-ecosystem records of a component (WM-SFT-007)
Organization, person and tool agent master records
Full intellectual-property and license-instrument legal model, including SPDX license text catalogues
Identifier naming scheme registries (PURL type registry, CPE dictionary governance, SWID reg-id authorities) except as used identifiers on a product or release
Dataset, AI-model-card and training-data masters except as referenced purpose or companion BOM
Hardware product and HWID tag masters (ISO/IEC 19770-6) except where firmware is the offered software
CVE, CWE and vulnerability-catalogue masters; this model records only product affectation and VEX status
Generic IT infrastructure, network, and non-software CMDB CIs
Source-control commit graphs, issue trackers and CI pipeline definitions as first-class objects (build formulation is provenance of a release only)
Entitlement commerce, metering and ISO/IEC 19770-3 entitlement schema as a legal or billing master
EU Cyber Resilience Act conformity-assessment dossiers and notified-body certificates

boundary_notes.distinction: A software product is the offered capability (CSAF: any named deliverable; CoSWID software-meta.product and persistent-id; SPDX Package as a distributable unit). A release is a versioned publication of that product. A component or package instance is a constituent and is composed from WM-SFT-007 rather than remodelled here.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Operator-side deployed inventory and endpoint tags
boundary_notes.distinction: Producer-side catalogue records and operator-side deployed inventory are distinct ownership slices of the same product/release identity. SWID/CoSWID primary tags live with the installation; corpus tags describe pre-install media and are not deployed on the target.

SPDX 2.2.1 is ISO/IEC 5962:2021; SPDX 3.0.1 is the OMG-published System Package Data Exchange used here for software profile semantics. SPDX 3.1 is a 2026 release candidate expanding into hardware, safety and operations and is treated as emerging, not canonical.

CISA 2026 Minimum Elements replace NTIA 2021 as current multinational SBOM baseline guidance; they are not a conformance scheme and call out extra elements for AI and SaaS without fully specifying them.
License expressions and copyright text may appear on a release or SBOM as references into the intellectual-property model; this model does not own license semantics.
Firmware is in scope when it is the offered software product; device hardware identity is out of scope.
Location applies to download URIs, advisory distribution endpoints, and hosting environment of a deployed system, not to a product's abstract identity.

bundles.name: Product offering
bundles.description: Identify the software product as an offered capability, classify its purpose and delivery mode, and record producer-side entity roles without absorbing organization or license masters.
bundles.rationale: The offered product identity is referable independently of any one file, package manager record or deployed instance, so identity, family and edition grouping, producer roles and classification are held together and ahead of any versioned publication.

layers.name: Product identity and naming
layers.description: Capture master identity, global identifier crosswalks, and family/edition/SKU grouping for a software product.

findings.name: Product master identity
findings.description: A software product is a named deliverable that can be referred to independently of any one file, package manager record or deployed instance. CSAF defines product as any named deliverable regardless of origin, license model or distribution mode. CoSWID requires a globally unique tag-id for a software component release and a software-name, and distinguishes a persistent-id and product name that survive across versions. SPDX requires a unique spdxId IRI on every Element and a required name on Package.

data_elements.name: Product identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative master-system identifier in the producer product registry

data_elements.name: Product name
data_elements.description: Canonical human-facing product name

data_elements.name: Persistent product line identifier
data_elements.description: CoSWID persistent-id or equivalent linking versions of the same product

data_elements.name: Summary description
data_elements.description: Single-sentence summary suitable for catalogue display

data_elements.name: Assigning authority
data_elements.description: Organization or registry that assigned the master identifier

artifacts.name: Product registry record
artifacts.description: Producer catalogue identity record for the software offering, independent of any one release artifact.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the producer-assigned product-id from the product registry, with persistent-product-id grouping versions of the same product line.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this software product and which authority assigned it?
What canonical name and short summary should agents use when referring to this product independently of a version string?
Which persistent product-line identifier groups this offering with other versions, channels or editions that are the same product over time?

findings.name: Global identifier crosswalk
findings.description: The same product or release is routinely named by several governed identifiers: Package-URL (pkg:type/namespace/name@version), CPE 2.3, SWID/CoSWID tag-id, SPDX spdxId and packageUrl, and CSAF product identification helpers (CPE, PURL, hashes, SKUs, SBOM URLs, generic URIs). These are alignments, not a single universal key. PURL is ecosystem-native; CPE is vendor-product oriented for NVD matching; SWID tag-id must be globally unique and must not contain a double underscore. A date is not an identifier.

data_elements.name: Package URL
data_elements.description: ECMA-427 Package-URL for the product or release

data_elements.name: CPE name
data_elements.description: CPE 2.3 well-formed name when one exists

data_elements.name: SWID or CoSWID tag-id
data_elements.description: Globally unique tag identifier (UUID or text)

data_elements.name: SPDX element IRI
data_elements.description: spdxId of the root package or product element

data_elements.name: Stock keeping unit
data_elements.description: Commercial SKU from CSAF product identification helpers

data_elements.name: Identifier conflicts
data_elements.description: Recorded mismatches among aligned identifier schemes

artifacts.name: Identifier crosswalk map
artifacts.description: Set of aligned external identifiers for one product or release with scheme, value and assigning system.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the product or release it annotates; each entry keyed by scheme name plus identifier value (PURL, CPE 2.3, SWID tag-id, SPDX IRI, SKU).

questions.text: Which PURL, CPE 2.3 name, SWID tag-id, SPDX IRI and SKU currently identify this product or release, and which of them is populated versus explicitly unknown?
Which identifier schemes are valid for matching this product to SBOMs, vulnerability databases and CSAF product trees, and where do those schemes disagree?
What evidence shows that each external identifier was assigned by its governing system rather than inferred by a scanner?

findings.name: Family, edition, channel and SKU
findings.description: CoSWID software-meta separates product, product-family, edition, channel-type, colloquial-version and revision from the exact software-version. CSAF product trees use vendor/product/version branches, product groups and relationships among products. These group commercial variants (enterprise versus standard, OEM versus academic, LTS line) without treating each SKU as an unrelated product or collapsing them into a single version.

data_elements.name: Product family
data_elements.description: Family spanning client, server or related capabilities

data_elements.name: Edition
data_elements.description: Functional variation such as standard or enterprise

data_elements.name: Channel type
data_elements.description: Sales or licensing channel such as OEM, retail, academic or volume

data_elements.name: Colloquial version
data_elements.description: Informal line label such as a year or major train

data_elements.name: Product group identifier
data_elements.description: CSAF product group id when variants are grouped for advisory status

artifacts.name: Product tree branch
artifacts.description: Family/edition/channel branch locating this offering inside a producer product tree.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the CSAF product id or product group id within the producer product tree.

questions.text: Which product family, edition and colloquial version line does this offering belong to, and which sibling editions share the same code base?
Which distribution or licensing channel (OEM, academic, retail, volume or other) applies to this offering?
Which CSAF product group, if any, collects this product with related products for common advisory or remediation status?

layers.name: Producer roles and product classification
layers.description: Record who created, supplies and maintains the product, and what kind of software offering it is, without owning organization or IP masters.

findings.name: Creator, supplier and maintainer roles
findings.description: CoSWID requires an entity with role tag-creator and should record software-creator; other registered roles include aggregator, distributor, licensor and maintainer, each with optional reg-id URI. SPDX Artifact distinguishes originatedBy from suppliedBy. CISA 2026 renamed NTIA Supplier Name to Component Producer and separates SBOM Author from Component Producer. CycloneDX metadata separately records manufacturer, supplier and authors. These are role assignments onto an organization sibling, not duplicate org records.

data_elements.name: Software creator reference
data_elements.description: Organization that created the software

data_elements.name: Supplier or producer reference
data_elements.description: Organization that supplies the product (CISA component producer / SPDX suppliedBy)

data_elements.name: Maintainer reference
data_elements.description: Organization currently maintaining the product

data_elements.name: Tag or SBOM author reference
data_elements.description: Party that created the identification tag or SBOM, which may differ from the producer

data_elements.name: Entity registration URI
data_elements.description: CoSWID entity reg-id naming-authority URI

artifacts.name: Entity role set
artifacts.description: Role-to-organization assignments for creator, producer, maintainer, distributor and tag author.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by product or release identifier plus role name; each role points at an organization IRI with a CoSWID reg-id naming authority where available.

questions.text: Which organization is the software creator, which is the current supplier or component producer, and which is the maintainer?
Who created the SWID/CoSWID tag or SBOM for this product, and is that party different from the component producer?
What registration URI or naming authority identifies each claimed entity so that role assertions can be correlated across documents?

findings.name: Software purpose and delivery mode
findings.description: SPDX SoftwareArtifact records primaryPurpose and additionalPurpose. CycloneDX components can represent software, hardware devices, machine learning models, source code, configurations and services; CycloneDX Services describe external APIs a product may call. CISA 2026 states that minimum SBOM elements apply to all software including open-source, AI software and SaaS, while AI and SaaS may require additional elements. UNSPSC codes appear on CoSWID software-meta. Delivery mode (on-prem application, library, container, firmware-as-software, SaaS) is classification of the offering, not a separate product model.

data_elements.name: Primary software purpose
data_elements.description: SPDX SoftwarePurpose or equivalent primary purpose

data_elements.name: Additional purposes
data_elements.description: Secondary purposes of the artifact

data_elements.name: Delivery mode
data_elements.description: On-prem, SaaS, container, firmware, library or mixed

data_elements.name: UNSPSC code
data_elements.description: Eight-digit UNSPSC classification and version

data_elements.name: Declared service endpoints
data_elements.description: External service URIs the offering depends on when delivered as or with services

artifacts.name: Product classification record
artifacts.description: Purpose, delivery mode and commodity classification of the offering.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the product identifier; classification values carry their code list and version, such as the UNSPSC code plus code-list version.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of this software offering and which additional purposes apply?
Is this offering delivered as installable software, a library, a container, firmware-as-software, SaaS, or a mix, and which extra transparency elements does that mode require?
Which external service endpoints, if any, are part of the offered product's runtime trust boundary?
What UNSPSC commodity code and code-list version classify this software product?

bundles.name: Release and publication
bundles.description: Describe versioned publications of a product, their channels, rare lifecycle events such as yank and metadata-only tag revision, and integrity plus build provenance of the distributable artifacts.
bundles.rationale: Version, channel and publication state change on their own clock and independently of product identity, and integrity plus build provenance attach to the published artifact rather than to the abstract offering.

layers.name: Versioning, channels and publication events
layers.description: Record how a release is numbered, channelled, published, withdrawn or patched.

findings.name: Version scheme, string and channel
findings.description: CoSWID records software-version plus a registered version-scheme (multipartnumeric, alphanumeric, decimal, semver and others) and optional media queries for target platform. SPDX Package has packageVersion, releaseTime and downloadLocation. CSAF versions may be integer or semantic and product version ranges use vers. Channels, pre-release labels (CoSWID revision such as RC or Beta) and colloquial versions must not be confused with the exact version string. A version string is not a timestamp; releaseTime is a separate clock.

data_elements.name: Release identifier
data_elements.description: Master identifier of this published version

data_elements.name: Version string
data_elements.description: Exact software-version or packageVersion

data_elements.name: Version scheme
data_elements.description: Registered scheme such as semver or multipartnumeric

data_elements.name: Release channel
data_elements.description: Stable, LTS, beta, nightly or vendor channel name

data_elements.name: Target media query
data_elements.description: CoSWID media query hint for applicable platforms

data_elements.name: Download location
data_elements.description: URI from which this release is obtained

artifacts.name: Release manifest
artifacts.description: Publication record for one version on one channel, including scheme and download locator.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by release-id, with version-string plus its declared version-scheme and channel as the governed serial.

questions.text: What is the master release identifier, exact version string and version scheme for this publication?
Which release channel and pre-release or revision label apply, and is this the same product line as the stable channel?
Where is this release obtained, and which target platforms or media queries constrain its applicability?

findings.name: Publication, withdrawal and yank
findings.description: ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 frames supply, operation, maintenance and disposal of software products. CoSWID models deployment, installation, patching, upgrading and removal. SPDX records releaseTime and validUntilTime. CSAF document tracking records initial_release_date, current_release_date, revision history and status including draft versus released. A published version may later be withdrawn or yanked from a channel without deleting historical identity, because exposure analysis still needs the withdrawn release. Tag-version may increase to correct metadata without changing software-version.

data_elements.name: Publication status
data_elements.description: draft, published, withdrawn, yanked or superseded

data_elements.name: Release event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 event time the version became available on the channel

data_elements.name: Withdrawal event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 event time the version was pulled if applicable

data_elements.name: Superseded release reference
data_elements.description: Prior release this one supersedes (CoSWID rel=supersedes)

data_elements.name: Tag revision number
data_elements.description: CoSWID tag-version; increases when the tag is corrected without a new software version

data_elements.name: Observation time
data_elements.description: When this publication state was observed or ingested

artifacts.name: Publication event log
artifacts.description: Time-ordered publication, withdrawal, yank and supersession events for a release line.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by release line; each entry keyed by release-id plus event kind and RFC 3339 event time.

questions.text: Is this release currently published, withdrawn, yanked, superseded or still draft on the stated channel?
At what event time was the release published or withdrawn, and at what separate observation or ingestion time was that fact recorded?
Has the identification tag been revised without a new software version, and which prior release does this version supersede?

findings.name: Patch versus upgrade and tag types
findings.description: CoSWID and NISTIR 8060 define four tag types used at different lifecycle points: corpus (pre-install media), primary (installed component), patch (incremental fix that MUST NOT change software-version) and supplemental (site-added metadata). Patch tags MUST link with rel=patches to the patched software. Upgrade replaces primary tags and changes version metadata. This distinction is a frequent omission in product catalogues that only store version strings.

data_elements.name: Tag type
data_elements.description: corpus, primary, patch or supplemental

data_elements.name: Patched release reference
data_elements.description: Release this patch applies to

data_elements.name: Patch changes version flag
data_elements.description: Must be false for a CoSWID patch tag

data_elements.name: Corpus installation media
data_elements.description: Pre-install package or installer location

artifacts.name: SWID or CoSWID tag
artifacts.description: Lifecycle-typed software identification tag for corpus, primary, patch or supplemental state.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the globally unique tag-id, which must not contain a double underscore, with tag-version as the metadata revision serial.

questions.text: Is the current identification record a corpus, primary, patch or supplemental tag, and where is it supposed to reside (media versus endpoint versus operator overlay)?
If this is a patch, which release does it patch, and does the patch illegally change the software-version?
If this is a pre-install corpus record, which installation media or package installer does it describe?

layers.name: Integrity and release provenance
layers.description: Bind hashes, signatures and build/release timestamps to a published artifact, separating event time from SBOM or inventory observation time.

findings.name: Hashes, content identifiers and signatures
findings.description: CISA 2026 adds Component Hash Value and Algorithm as minimum SBOM elements. CoSWID hash-entry uses IANA Named Information hash algorithms with raw hash bytes; unknown algorithm is 0. SPDX verifiedUsing and contentIdentifier carry integrity methods. CSAF product identification helpers include hashes and discourage MD5 or SHA-1 as the only algorithm. CycloneDX components include hashes and independently signable annotations. Integrity of the SBOM or advisory document is distinct from integrity of the software artifact.

data_elements.name: Hash algorithm
data_elements.description: IANA or CISA-recognized hash algorithm

data_elements.name: Hash value
data_elements.description: Digest of the artifact

data_elements.name: Content identifier
data_elements.description: SPDX contentIdentifier or equivalent gitoid/SWHID

data_elements.name: Signature reference
data_elements.description: Detached or embedded signature of artifact or SBOM

data_elements.name: SBOM author signature
data_elements.description: CISA 2026 SBOM Author Signature when present

artifacts.name: Artifact digest set
artifacts.description: Algorithm/value pairs and signatures covering the release artifact and optionally its SBOM.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the artifact it covers plus hash algorithm; SBOM or advisory document digests are kept distinct from software artifact digests.

questions.text: What hash algorithms and values identify this release artifact, and is a current algorithm present rather than MD5 or SHA-1 alone?
What content identifier (SPDX contentIdentifier, gitoid, SWHID or equivalent) is bound to the artifact bytes?
Is the artifact or its SBOM signed, by whom, and does a CISA 2026 SBOM Author Signature exist distinct from the component producer?

findings.name: Build and release provenance
findings.description: SPDX Artifact records builtTime, releaseTime, originatedBy, suppliedBy and creationInfo (required). CycloneDX Formulation describes declared and observed manufacturing or deployment workflows; Citations record who contributed which BOM facts and when. CoSWID evidence is generated on-device and is mutually exclusive with payload. Event time of the build or release must be stored separately from observation or ingestion time of the SBOM or inventory record. Deep CI pipeline models are out of scope; only provenance needed to operate the product record is in scope.

data_elements.name: Built time
data_elements.description: Event time the releasable artifact was built

data_elements.name: Release time
data_elements.description: Event time the artifact was released

data_elements.name: Document creation time
data_elements.description: Observation time the SBOM or tag was created

data_elements.name: Originated-by agent
data_elements.description: SPDX originatedBy agent

data_elements.name: Formulation or build id
data_elements.description: Declared or observed build formula identifier

data_elements.name: Ingestion time
data_elements.description: When this Dimension ingested the provenance record

artifacts.name: Release provenance statement
artifacts.description: Build and release event timestamps plus creating agents, distinct from document ingestion time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by release-id plus creating agent, with build and release event times held separately from document creation and ingestion time.

questions.text: When was this artifact built and when was it released, using RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and an explicit offset?
Which agent originated the artifact, which supplied it, and which tool or person created the SBOM or tag?
What is the observation or ingestion time of this provenance record, and how does it differ from build and release event time?

bundles.name: Composition and transparency
bundles.description: Describe the product- or release-grain bill of materials, dependency edges, and completeness or known-unknown statements, composing component nodes from WM-SFT-007.
bundles.rationale: An SBOM document is evidence about a release rather than the release itself, and dependency plus completeness statements must stay separable from the component masters they point at in WM-SFT-007.

layers.name: SBOM document and contained graph
layers.description: Govern SBOM metadata and the contained-component graph at release grain.

findings.name: SBOM authorship, type and generation context
findings.description: SPDX Sbom is a Bom describing a single package, with sbomType values analyzed, build, deployed, design, runtime and source as defined by CISA SBOM types. CycloneDX metadata.lifecycles and metadata.component identify the subject and lifecycle. CISA 2026 adds SBOM Author (distinct from Component Producer), SBOM Tool Name/Version, SBOM Generation Context, SBOM Data Format Name/Version, SBOM Version and Author Signature. An SBOM document is evidence about a release, not the product itself.

data_elements.name: SBOM identifier
data_elements.description: Master id of the SBOM document

data_elements.name: SBOM type
data_elements.description: design, source, build, analyzed, deployed, runtime or combination

data_elements.name: SBOM data format and version
data_elements.description: SPDX or CycloneDX name and spec version as a projection

data_elements.name: SBOM author
data_elements.description: CISA SBOM Author

data_elements.name: SBOM tool name and version
data_elements.description: Tool that generated the SBOM

data_elements.name: Generation context
data_elements.description: CISA SBOM Generation Context

data_elements.name: SBOM created timestamp
data_elements.description: Document timestamp, not the software releaseTime

artifacts.name: Software bill of materials document
artifacts.description: SBOM describing one release or product root, including authorship and type metadata.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by sbom-id (SPDX spdxId or CycloneDX BOM identity), with SBOM Version as the document serial and the described release as the subject.

questions.text: Who authored this SBOM, with which tool and generation context, and is that author different from the component producer?
Which SBOM types apply (design, source, build, analyzed, deployed, runtime) and which data format projection and document version is this?
When was the SBOM document created, and how does that observation time differ from the described software's releaseTime?

findings.name: Contained components at product grain
findings.description: A release is composed of components or packages. SPDX relationships and CycloneDX components plus compositions describe containment. CISA 2026 requires Component Name, Component Version, Component Identifiers, Component Producer, Component Hash and Component License as baseline fields. This model stores the graph at product/release grain and COMPOSE-links each component node to WM-SFT-007 rather than duplicating package internals, files or ecosystem metadata.

data_elements.name: Root component reference
data_elements.description: The product or release root the SBOM describes

data_elements.name: Contained component references
data_elements.description: WM-SFT-007 component or package identifiers contained by the release

data_elements.name: Containment relationship type
data_elements.description: contains, describes or equivalent

data_elements.name: Component producer name
data_elements.description: CISA Component Producer on each contained node

data_elements.name: Component license reference
data_elements.description: Reference into the intellectual-property model, not a local license text

artifacts.name: Release composition graph
artifacts.description: Typed containment edges from a release root to component nodes owned by WM-SFT-007.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the release root element; each edge keyed by source element, relationship type and target component IRI mastered in WM-SFT-007.

questions.text: Which element is the root product or package this bill of materials describes?
Which component or package records (WM-SFT-007) are contained in this release, and with which containment relationship?
Which intellectual-property records are referenced as component licenses, without copying license legal text into this model?

layers.name: Dependencies and completeness
layers.description: Record declared needs, constraint ranges and honest coverage including known unknowns.

findings.name: Declared dependencies and constraints
findings.description: CycloneDX dependency graphs represent direct and transitive relationships among components and services. CoSWID link rel=requires with use=required|optional|recommended models install-time needs. CSAF and PURL ecosystems use vers ranges. A declared dependency is not the same as a resolved release; resolution may pin a concrete WM-SFT-007 package or a WM-SFT-001 release. Scope (compile, runtime, test, optional) is an operating constraint.

data_elements.name: Dependency identifier
data_elements.description: Local id of the declared need

data_elements.name: Depends-on reference
data_elements.description: Target product, release or WM-SFT-007 component

data_elements.name: Version constraint
data_elements.description: vers range or ecosystem constraint

data_elements.name: Dependency scope
data_elements.description: required, optional, recommended, runtime, test or similar

data_elements.name: Resolved release reference
data_elements.description: Concrete release satisfying the constraint if known

data_elements.name: Direct or transitive
data_elements.description: Graph depth classification

artifacts.name: Dependency graph
artifacts.description: Declared and optionally resolved dependency edges for a release.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the release under analysis; each edge keyed by dependency-id with its depends-on target, version constraint and scope.

questions.text: Which other products, releases or components does this release declare a need for, and are those edges direct or transitive?
What version constraint or vers range applies, and which concrete release currently resolves it?
Is each dependency required, optional or recommended, and in which scope (runtime, test or install) does it apply?

findings.name: Coverage, completeness and known unknowns
findings.description: CISA 2026 replaces NTIA Depth with Coverage (horizontal and vertical breadth) and requires explicitly identifying unknown information. CycloneDX compositions aggregate completeness as complete, incomplete, incomplete first-party only, incomplete third-party only or unknown. SPDX Sbom may carry multiple sbomTypes. An SBOM that omits unknowns is less operable than one that marks them. Completeness is a quality measurement of the composition evidence, not of the software.

data_elements.name: Coverage statement
data_elements.description: Horizontal and vertical coverage claimed

data_elements.name: Completeness aggregate
data_elements.description: CycloneDX composition aggregate value

data_elements.name: Known unknowns
data_elements.description: Explicit unknown component, license or dependency slots

data_elements.name: First-party completeness
data_elements.description: Whether first-party content is complete

data_elements.name: Third-party completeness
data_elements.description: Whether third-party content is complete

artifacts.name: Completeness declaration
artifacts.description: Machine-readable coverage and known-unknown statement for an SBOM or composition.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the SBOM or composition it qualifies, carrying the aggregate value and explicit known-unknown slots rather than omissions.

questions.text: What completeness aggregate applies to this composition, and is first-party or third-party content incomplete?
Which component, dependency, license or identifier fields are explicitly unknown rather than omitted?
What horizontal and vertical coverage does the producer claim relative to CISA 2026 Coverage, and what is out of that claim?

bundles.name: Support and exposure
bundles.description: Govern support and end-of-life of a product or release line, and the advisories plus VEX status that map vulnerabilities onto products without owning the vulnerability catalogue.
bundles.rationale: Support declarations and advisory affectation are producer statements about products and releases that run on their own clocks, and they must be recorded without absorbing the CVE or CWE catalogues they cite.

layers.name: Support lifecycle and disposal
layers.description: Record support level, end dates and disposal of the product or release train.

findings.name: Support level, valid-until and end of life
findings.description: SPDX Artifact supportLevel and validUntilTime state until when an artifact can be used before reassessment. ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 includes maintenance, operation and disposal processes and does not prescribe a single lifecycle model. Commercial practice distinguishes end of sale, end of maintenance, end of support and end of life; those labels are producer declarations, not 12207 process names. A product may still be deployed after validUntilTime; that is an operator risk state, not automatic deletion of the record.

data_elements.name: Support level
data_elements.description: SPDX SupportType or producer support label

data_elements.name: Valid-until time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time after which use must be reassessed

data_elements.name: End-of-life announced at
data_elements.description: Event time of the producer EOL announcement

data_elements.name: End-of-life effective at
data_elements.description: Event time support actually ends

data_elements.name: 12207 process alignment
data_elements.description: supply, operation, maintenance or disposal alignment, not a claim of 12207 conformance

artifacts.name: Support and lifecycle record
artifacts.description: Producer-declared support level and end dates for a product or release line.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by product or release line identifier plus the producer organization declaring the support level.

questions.text: What support level currently applies to this product or release line, and is it still within valid-until time?
When was end of life announced, when does support actually end, and how do those event times differ from the date the record was ingested?
Which 12207-aligned process (maintenance, operation or disposal) is the product in, without claiming conformance to ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207?
Which producer or maintainer organization is accountable for the support declaration?

layers.name: Advisories and exploitability
layers.description: Map CSAF advisories and VEX product status onto products and releases.

findings.name: Advisory identity, tracking and distribution
findings.description: CSAF 2.0 is the OASIS language for creating, updating and exchanging security advisories as structured information on products, vulnerabilities and impact or remediation status. Document tracking requires an ID, version, status, revision history, publisher (with namespace and issuing authority) and optional TLP. Profiles include CSAF Base, Security incident response, Informational Advisory, Security Advisory and VEX. Distribution rules cover well-known provider-metadata, security.txt, TLS, signatures and TLP labels. Advisory identity is not a CVE id, though a CSAF vulnerability may cite one.

data_elements.name: Advisory tracking identifier
data_elements.description: CSAF document.tracking.id

data_elements.name: Advisory document version
data_elements.description: Integer or semantic document version

data_elements.name: Advisory status
data_elements.description: draft, final, interim or withdrawn as used by tracking.status

data_elements.name: Publisher namespace
data_elements.description: CSAF publisher.namespace

data_elements.name: TLP label
data_elements.description: Traffic Light Protocol distribution label

data_elements.name: Document category or profile
data_elements.description: csaf_base, security_advisory, vex or other profile

artifacts.name: CSAF advisory document
artifacts.description: Machine-readable security advisory or VEX document with tracking metadata.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by document.tracking.id within the publisher namespace, with document version and revision history as the serial.

questions.text: What is the CSAF tracking identifier, document version and profile of this advisory?
Which publisher namespace and issuing authority released this advisory, and is that party the product vendor, a coordinator or a finder?
What TLP label and distribution constraints apply, and is the document in draft, interim, final or withdrawn status?

findings.name: Product status and VEX assertions
findings.description: CSAF product_status maps products to known_affected, known_not_affected, fixed, under_investigation and related first/last affected and first fixed lists. VEX (CSAF Profile 5) lets a supplier assert whether a product is affected by a named vulnerability, which is essential when consuming SBOMs. Flags carry VEX justification codes. This model stores affectation of local products and releases; it does not own CVE records. Contradicting product status is a CSAF mandatory-test failure and must be treated as a validation error.

data_elements.name: Affected product references
data_elements.description: Local products or releases listed as known_affected

data_elements.name: Not-affected product references
data_elements.description: Products asserted known_not_affected

data_elements.name: Fixed product references
data_elements.description: Products listed as fixed

data_elements.name: VEX status
data_elements.description: affected, not_affected, fixed, under_investigation

data_elements.name: VEX justification
data_elements.description: Status justification code when not affected

data_elements.name: Cited CVE
data_elements.description: External CVE identifier referenced, not mastered here

artifacts.name: VEX product-status statement
artifacts.description: Per-product exploitability assertion binding an advisory to local product and release identifiers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by advisory tracking id plus the local product or release identifier the status applies to; contradicting statuses are a validation error.

questions.text: Which local products or releases are known affected, known not affected, fixed or under investigation for this advisory?
If the product is not affected, what VEX justification supports that assertion?
Which cited CVE or vulnerability identifiers does this assertion bind to, as external references rather than local masters?

findings.name: Remediation, entitlements and restart
findings.description: CSAF remediations carry category, date, details, product or group ids, URL, restart-required and entitlements. Entitlements here are access gates on a remediation (who may obtain the fix), not the intellectual-property license of the software. CoSWID activation-status and entitlement-key similarly record install-time activation without storing unprotected license secrets. Restart-required is an operational constraint on deployed systems.

data_elements.name: Remediation category
data_elements.description: vendor_fix, workaround, mitigation, none_available or no_fix_planned

data_elements.name: Remediation URL
data_elements.description: Locator of the fix or guidance

data_elements.name: Restart required
data_elements.description: Whether and how a restart is required

data_elements.name: Remediation entitlements
data_elements.description: Who is entitled to obtain the fix

data_elements.name: Activation status
data_elements.description: trial, licensed, unlicensed or similar CoSWID activation-status

artifacts.name: Remediation record
artifacts.description: Fix, workaround or mitigation bound to products, with entitlement and restart constraints.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by advisory tracking id plus remediation category and the product or product group ids it addresses.

questions.text: What remediation category and URL are offered for the affected products, and on which date was that remediation published?
Does applying the remediation require a restart, and of what kind?
Which entitlements gate access to the fix, and what activation status applies to the installed product?

bundles.name: Operation and inventory
bundles.description: Describe operator-owned deployed systems that run a release, their hosting environments, and discovery evidence, without absorbing a general CMDB or infrastructure model.
bundles.rationale: Deployed installations are operator-owned records whose stewardship, access rules and lifecycle differ from the producer catalogue, so they are bundled apart from product and release publication.

layers.name: Deployed system, environment and evidence
layers.description: Record running installations, hosting context and how presence was observed.

findings.name: Deployed system running a release
findings.description: ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 includes operation of software products. CoSWID lifecycle requires that a primary tag be installed with the software and removed on uninstall, creating correspondence between installed software and tags. CycloneDX deployed and runtime SBOM types inventory what is present on a system, including dynamically loaded components and external call-outs. A deployed system is an operator-owned instance that runs one or more releases; it is not the product catalogue record. Criticality and purpose are operator classifications.

data_elements.name: Deployed system identifier
data_elements.description: Operator master identifier of the instance

data_elements.name: Running release reference
data_elements.description: WM-SFT-001 release this system currently runs

data_elements.name: Operator organization reference
data_elements.description: Organization that operates the system

data_elements.name: System purpose
data_elements.description: Why the operator runs this instance

data_elements.name: Criticality
data_elements.description: Operator criticality classification

data_elements.name: Deployed event time
data_elements.description: When the release went live in this instance

data_elements.name: Decommissioned event time
data_elements.description: When the instance was retired if applicable

artifacts.name: Operations inventory record
artifacts.description: Operator-owned record of a running system and the releases it executes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the operator system-id assigned by the inventory system, linked to the release identifiers it runs.

questions.text: What is the operator master identifier of this deployed system, and which organization operates it?
Which product releases currently run on this system, and for what purpose and criticality?
When was this system deployed or decommissioned, as event times distinct from inventory observation time?

findings.name: Hosting environment and discovery evidence
findings.description: CoSWID payload lists artifacts that compose installable or installed software and is mutually exclusive with evidence, which is produced on the endpoint by discovery. Evidence may include files, processes and resources actually observed. CycloneDX runtime SBOMs capture components present at execution. Environment is a hosting context (type, platform, location reference) for the deployed system, referenced rather than modelled as full infrastructure. Supplemental tags let operators add site metadata without altering producer primary tags.

data_elements.name: Environment identifier
data_elements.description: Operator identifier of the hosting context

data_elements.name: Environment type
data_elements.description: production, staging, development, edge or similar

data_elements.name: Platform
data_elements.description: OS, architecture or orchestration platform

data_elements.name: Location reference
data_elements.description: Geographic or data-centre location of the environment

data_elements.name: Evidence collected at
data_elements.description: Observation time of endpoint discovery

data_elements.name: Payload or evidence mode
data_elements.description: Whether the tag carries producer payload or on-device evidence

data_elements.name: Discovered file hashes
data_elements.description: Hashes observed on the endpoint for correlation

artifacts.name: Endpoint discovery evidence
artifacts.description: On-device evidence or runtime SBOM placing a release in a hosting environment.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by system-id plus evidence collection observation time; observed hashes correlate the evidence to a published release digest set.

questions.text: In which environment type, platform and location is this deployed system hosted?
Was presence established from producer payload, on-device evidence, or a runtime SBOM, and when was that observation collected?
Which file or image hashes were observed on the endpoint, and do they match the published release digest set?
Which operator role may read or update this inventory evidence, given that deployment detail is omitted from public product catalogues?

functions.name: Register product
functions.description: Create the producer-side software product identity, persistent product-line id, classification and entity-role assignments.
inputs: Persistent product-line identifier where one exists
Creator, supplier and maintainer organization references
preconditions: An authoritative master-system identifier is available from the producer product registry, or a governed global identifier or locally assigned UUID/ULID stands in for it
effects: Producer-side product identity, classification and role assignments exist and can be referenced by releases

functions.name: Publish release
functions.description: Publish a versioned release on a channel with version scheme, download location, hashes and release event time.
preconditions: At least one current-algorithm hash is available for the release artifact
effects: A versioned publication exists on the stated channel with release event time recorded separately from observation time

functions.name: Revise identification tag
functions.description: Increment tag-version to correct metadata without changing software-version.
effects: Tag metadata is corrected without creating a new software version

functions.name: Withdraw or yank release
functions.description: Mark a published version withdrawn or yanked while retaining historical identity for exposure analysis.
preconditions: The release was previously published on the channel
effects: The version is marked withdrawn or yanked and its historical identity is retained for exposure matching

functions.name: Apply patch tag
functions.description: Install a patch tag linked with rel=patches that must not change software-version, or perform an upgrade that replaces primary tags.
outputs: Patch tag linked with rel=patches, or replaced primary tags after an upgrade
preconditions: A patch tag must not change software-version
effects: Installed state reflects the patch or upgrade
Primary tags are replaced when the version changes

functions.name: Generate SBOM
functions.description: Produce a design, source, build, analyzed, deployed or runtime SBOM for a release, recording author, tool, generation context, format and known unknowns.
effects: SBOM evidence exists for the release with author, tool, type, format and explicit known unknowns recorded

functions.name: Declare and resolve dependency
functions.description: Record a declared constraint onto another component or release and optionally pin a resolved release.
effects: A declared need is recorded and may be pinned to a concrete resolved release

functions.name: Announce support change or end of life
functions.description: Set support level, valid-until time and end-of-life announcement versus effective times for a product or release line.
effects: Support state is published with announcement and effective event times distinct from ingestion time

functions.name: Issue advisory
functions.description: Publish a CSAF document with tracking identity, publisher authority, TLP and product tree.
preconditions: A document tracking identifier, version and status are assigned
effects: A machine-readable advisory exists with revision history and distribution constraints

functions.name: Assert VEX status
functions.description: Bind known_affected, known_not_affected, fixed or under_investigation status and justifications to local products and releases.
preconditions: Product status assignments must not contradict each other
effects: Exploitability status is bound to local products and releases without mastering the vulnerability record

functions.name: Record deployment
functions.description: Create an operator-owned deployed system running a release in an environment, with deploy event time distinct from discovery observation time.
effects: An operator-owned deployed system is recorded with deploy event time distinct from discovery observation time

functions.name: Collect inventory evidence
functions.description: Capture on-device evidence or a runtime SBOM, including observed hashes, without modifying producer primary tags; supplemental tags may hold site metadata.
inputs: Endpoint discovery output or runtime SBOM
preconditions: Producer primary tags are not modified; site metadata goes into supplemental tags
effects: Observed presence of releases is recorded with an evidence collection observation time

functions.name: Match advisory to inventory
functions.description: Match CSAF product identification helpers and VEX status to SBOM components and deployed releases (CSAF SBOM matching and asset matching systems).
effects: Affected deployed releases are identified for remediation

functions.name: Verify artifact integrity
functions.description: Compare published hashes and signatures to downloaded artifacts or endpoint evidence using current hash algorithms.
inputs: Downloaded artifact or endpoint evidence hashes
preconditions: A current hash algorithm is used; MD5 or SHA-1 alone is not sufficient
effects: Artifact bytes are confirmed against, or flagged as mismatching, the published release

functions.name: Retire deployment
functions.description: Decommission a deployed system and remove corresponding primary, patch and supplemental tags per the SWID/CoSWID lifecycle.
effects: Primary, patch and supplemental tags are removed per the SWID/CoSWID lifecycle
The deployed system is marked decommissioned

functions.name: Disclose SBOM or inventory
functions.description: Share a catalogue, SBOM or operator inventory under TLP, contractual and access-scope rules, auditing disclosure separately from public product pages.
outputs: Disclosure export carrying its TLP label and recipient scope
preconditions: An explicit scope grant from the owning steward exists for non-public content
effects: The disclosure is recorded in the audit log separately from public product pages

composition.purpose: A software product or release is composed of components or packages whose internal identity, files and ecosystem records are mastered in WM-SFT-007; this model keeps only the product-grain graph, constraint edges and SBOM evidence. Known relation states that a software product is composed of components or packages; SPDX Package and CycloneDX components are the interchange shapes of those nodes.

Product and release records align to SPDX Package/SoftwareArtifact; SBOM documents align to SPDX Sbom; supportLevel and validUntilTime align to support lifecycle. Alignment is not conformance. SPDX 3.0.1 is the current Software profile used for SBOM, package identity, provenance and support fields.

BOM metadata, components, services, dependencies, compositions, vulnerabilities/VEX, formulation and citations are interchange alignments for composition, completeness and provenance. CISA 2026 names SPDX and CycloneDX as the two widely used SBOM data formats.

Installed presence, tag types, entity roles, links, hashes and software-meta product-family fields align to SWID/CoSWID. RFC 9393 warns the implicit information model may diverge from ISO 19770-2 over time. SWID is the ISO software identification tag; CoSWID is the IETF concise encoding used for constrained endpoints and attestation.

Advisory, VEX, product tree, product status, remediations and TLP distribution align to CSAF; CSAF product is broader than software and extra non-software branches are out of scope. CSAF is the normative language for machine-readable security advisories and VEX.

composition.target: CISA 2026 Minimum Elements for an SBOM
composition.purpose: SBOM baseline fields, coverage, known unknowns, hashes, licenses, author versus producer and generation context align to CISA 2026 guidance without treating that guidance as a certifiable scheme. CISA 2026 updates and replaces the NTIA 2021 SBOM minimum elements.

PURL is a governed global identifier for packages and is used in SPDX, CycloneDX, CSAF helpers and CVE records; scheme registries remain a sibling identifier-naming concern. PURL is the cross-ecosystem package identifier adopted by SBOM and advisory standards.

Acquisition, supply, development, operation, maintenance and disposal name the process backdrop for product and deployed-system lifecycle; this model does not implement 12207 process assessment. 12207:2026 is the current international software life cycle process framework.

Creator, supplier, maintainer, operator, publisher and tag-author are role assignments onto organization records; this model does not master organizations. Entity roles in CoSWID, SPDX Agent, CSAF publisher and operator of a deployed system all point outside the software product.

Component and product licenses, copyright text and entitlement legal terms reference the IP model; CISA 2026 Component License is stored as a pointer plus expression string, not as a license master. License semantics are intellectual property, not software identity.

PURL types, CPE dictionary entries, SWID reg-id authorities and SPDX external identifier types are scheme records owned by the identifier-naming model; this model stores values and scheme names only. Identifier schemes are reusable across domains and must not be duplicated per product.

Datasets produced or consumed by a deployed system, and AI training or evaluation data called out by CISA AI SBOM extras, are referenced rather than modelled. CISA notes AI software may need additional SBOM elements; dataset masters belong in the dataset model.

owner_package_requirements: The owning package MUST publish AGENTS.md carrying Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any create or update is attempted.

The owning package MUST keep producer stewardship (product, release, published SBOM, advisories) separate from operator stewardship (deployed systems, environments, supplemental tags, inventory evidence).
The owning package MUST reference the organization, intellectual-property, identifier-naming and dataset models rather than mastering them locally, and MUST COMPOSE component nodes from WM-SFT-007.
dimension.namespace_guidance: This model is namespaced as vr.wm-sft-001 (WM-SFT-001). Component and package internals belong to the WM-SFT-007 namespace; organizations, license instruments, identifier schemes and datasets stay in their sibling namespaces and are addressed by IRI reference, never copied into this namespace.
registry_links: WM-SFT-007 — software component or package model targeted by COMPOSE

canonicalization_rules: All time values are canonicalized to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z, with event time stored separately from observation or ingestion time.

Identifiers are canonicalized to the highest available identity priority: master-system identifier, then governed global identifier (spdxId, PURL, CPE 2.3, CSAF product id, SWID/CoSWID tag-id), then a locally assigned UUID or ULID.
Version strings are recorded verbatim alongside their declared version scheme and are never rewritten into another scheme; a version string is not a timestamp and a date is not an identifier.
patch_rules: A patch record MUST NOT change software-version; an upgrade that changes the version replaces primary tags instead.
Metadata-only corrections increment tag-version and leave software-version untouched.
Withdrawal, yank and supersession are recorded as status changes plus event-log entries; they never erase the historical release identity.
compatibility_rules: External standards are alignments, not conformance; adding or retiring a format projection MUST NOT change model semantics.
SPDX 2.2.1 (ISO/IEC 5962:2021), SPDX 3.0.1 and CycloneDX 1.7 projections coexist; SPDX 3.1 RC is treated as emerging and excluded from the canonical structure.
New baseline elements, including CISA 2026 additions and the flagged AI and SaaS extras, are added as fields that can carry an explicit known-unknown value rather than being silently omitted.

identity_priority: authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the producing organization's product or package registry for products and releases, or by the operator's inventory system for deployed systems
governed global identifier or IRI such as an SPDX spdxId, Package-URL, CPE 2.3 name, CSAF product id or SWID/CoSWID tag-id
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension only when no master-system or governed global identifier is available
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values SHALL be recorded in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Event time (builtTime, releaseTime, published or withdrawn, advisory initial_release_date, deployed or decommissioned, end-of-life effective) SHALL be stored separately from observation or ingestion time (SBOM created timestamp, CoSWID evidence collection, CSAF current_release_date of a document revision, catalogue ingestion). A date is not an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named by the owning product or release identifier plus the governed sequence value of that artifact class: software-version with its declared version-scheme for release manifests, CoSWID tag-version for identification tags, SBOM Version for SBOM documents, and CSAF document version with revision history for advisories. A date or timestamp MUST NOT be used as the serial.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Release artifacts and SBOM or advisory documents SHALL carry at least one current-algorithm hash (CISA 2026 Component Hash; CoSWID IANA Named Information algorithms; SPDX verifiedUsing). Signatures and CISA SBOM Author Signature are recorded when present. MD5 or SHA-1 MUST NOT be the only hash. Producer payload hashes and operator evidence hashes are distinct measurements.

policies: Split stewardship: the producing organization owns product, release, SBOM-as-published and producer advisories; the operator owns deployed systems, environments, supplemental tags and inventory evidence.
Known unknowns SHALL be explicit. Omitting a CISA 2026 field is not equivalent to recording that the field is unknown.
Public product catalogue projections SHALL omit operator inventory, environment location and entitlement secrets. SBOM and advisory sharing follow TLP and contractual disclosure, with audit.
Withdrawn, yanked and end-of-support releases SHALL be retained for exposure matching until the retention period expires; publication status must not erase identity.
License legal text and organization master data SHALL be referenced, not copied, from sibling models.
Patch records MUST NOT silently change software-version; upgrades that change version replace primary tags.

read: Read public product and release catalogue fields
Read SBOM metadata and composition graphs according to disclosure scope
Read CSAF/VEX status for products the caller is entitled to see
Read operator inventory only within the operator's access scope
create: Create product identity and entity-role assignments
Create a release publication with hashes and event time
Create SBOM documents and declared dependency edges
Create CSAF advisories or VEX assertions
update: Update support level, valid-until and end-of-life dates
Revise tag-version metadata without changing software-version
Update VEX product status and remediations
Update running release pointers and discovery evidence on a deployed system
Correct identifier crosswalks and known-unknown flags
delete: Soft-delete or withdraw a release from a channel while retaining historical identity
Remove primary, patch and supplemental tags on decommission per CoSWID lifecycle
Hard-delete operator inventory according to retention and legal hold
Refuse hard-delete of a product still referenced by advisories or deployments unless those links are reassigned

roles.name: Product steward
responsibilities: Own producer-side product identity, family and classification
Assign creator, supplier and maintainer role references

roles.name: Release publisher
responsibilities: Attach hashes, signatures and download locations

roles.name: SBOM author
responsibilities: Generate SBOM documents with type, tool, generation context and known unknowns
Keep SBOM Author distinct from Component Producer when they differ
Disclose SBOMs under the applicable policy

roles.name: Operator
responsibilities: Own deployed systems, environments and inventory evidence
Install, patch, upgrade and remove software tags on endpoints
Apply remediations and record restart outcomes

roles.name: PSIRT advisory issuer
responsibilities: Issue CSAF documents and VEX assertions
Maintain publisher namespace, TLP and revision history
Map product status onto local product and release identifiers

roles.name: Catalogue access steward
responsibilities: Grant bundle, layer, finding and artifact scopes
Enforce retention, legal hold and exception handling

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Producer catalogue identity and published release metadata may be granted read to authenticated consumers of that producer; SBOM internals, operator inventory, environment locations, entitlement keys and non-WHITE TLP advisories require an explicit scope grant from the owning steward.
exceptions: Emergency vulnerability-response break-glass may grant time-bounded read of operator inventory and non-public advisories, with mandatory audit and expiry
Public open-source product catalogue pages may be world-readable while still withholding deployment and entitlement fields
audit_requirements: Log create, update, delete, disclosure and exception grants at finding and artifact grain with actor, action, event time and observation time
Retain access logs at least as long as the disclosed SBOM, advisory or inventory artifact
Record TLP label and recipient scope on every advisory or SBOM export

read_order: Read AGENTS.md for Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any create or update
Read the Specification URL for identity, lifecycle and composition rules
Read the Processes URL for publish, SBOM, advisory and deployment workflows
Read the Interface URL only as an access projection after the specification semantics are loaded

coverage.claim: Defensible, format-neutral coverage of software product identity, release publication, integrity and provenance, product-grain SBOM composition and dependencies, support and end-of-life, CSAF/VEX exposure, and operator deployment inventory, grounded in SPDX 3.0.1, RFC 9393/ISO 19770-2, CISA 2026 SBOM minimum elements, CycloneDX 1.7, CSAF 2.0, PURL/ECMA-427 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2026. External standards are alignments. Component internals, licenses, organizations, identifier schemes and datasets are sibling concerns. Completeness is not claimed.

checklist.notes: Master-system product and release ids, persistent-id, PURL, CPE, SWID tag-id, SPDX IRI and CSAF product id, with identity priority encoded in artifact rules.
Publication, yank, patch versus upgrade, CoSWID corpus/primary/patch/supplemental, 12207 operation/maintenance/disposal, support and EOL, deploy and decommission.
Contains, depends-on, patches, supersedes, runs, hosted-in, advisory-affects and entity roles; component nodes composed to WM-SFT-007.
RFC 3339 event versus observation/ingestion times for build, release, SBOM created, advisory tracking, deploy and EOL.
originatedBy/suppliedBy, SBOM author versus component producer, formulation/build id, CoSWID evidence versus payload, CycloneDX citations.
Producer owns catalogue and published SBOMs; operator owns inventory; tag-creator may differ from software-creator.
Hash algorithms, CSAF mandatory tests analogue (contradicting product status, unique product ids), known unknowns, patch-must-not-change-version, completeness aggregates.
TLP, catalogue versus inventory projections, entitlement gates on remediations, deny-by-default scopes at bundle/layer/finding/artifact.
Withdrawn releases retained for exposure matching; CoSWID tag removal on uninstall; hard-delete constrained by advisory and deployment references.
Alignments to SPDX, CycloneDX, SWID/CoSWID, CSAF, CISA 2026 and PURL; identifier crosswalks and recorded conflicts; no conformance claim.
Release-grain SBOM graph, CycloneDX compositions, CISA coverage, COMPOSE to WM-SFT-007.
CSAF tracking, VEX product status, remediations, matching to inventory.
Deployed system, environment, runtime/deployed SBOM types and on-device evidence.

known_omissions: ISO/IEC 19770-2 XML schema annexes were not retrieved in full; CoSWID/RFC 9393 and NISTIR 8060 paraphrases carry the tag information model used here.

CISA 2026 PDF body was retrieved as a file but not fully field-extracted; new-element names come from the official landing page and partner summaries and should be re-checked against the PDF tables before implementation.
ISO/IEC 19770-3 entitlement schema, ISO/IEC 19770-1 SAM processes and ISO/IEC 19770-6 HWID are not modelled.
EU Cyber Resilience Act and BSI TR-03183-2 SBOM requirements are regional obligations not ingested as primary text in this run.
CISA Software Bill of Materials for AI — Minimum Elements (May 2026) and SaaS-specific extra elements are flagged as required extras, not expanded.
SLSA, in-toto and SPDX Build profile details are only represented as formulation/provenance stubs.
SPDX 3.1 RC (January 2026) hardware, safety and operations expansions are emerging and excluded from the canonical structure.
Commercial SKU/price-list, export-control classification and dual-use coding have no primary support here.
Product-line variability (feature flags, SPL) beyond edition/channel is a gap.
Full CPE 2.3 naming specification (NISTIR 7695) was cited via CSAF informative references, not fetched as a standalone primary.
conflicts: SPDX and CycloneDX are competing SBOM formats both recognized by CISA 2026; neither is the meta-model.
CPE vendor:product identity and PURL ecosystem identity often cannot be derived from each other; both may be absent.
NTIA 2021 Supplier Name versus CISA 2026 Component Producer versus SPDX originatedBy/suppliedBy versus CycloneDX manufacturer/supplier are overlapping but not identical roles.
RFC 9393 states SWID and CoSWID may diverge because they are maintained by different bodies.
CoSWID forbids a patch from changing software-version; many package ecosystems treat patches as new versions.
CSAF product includes hardware and specifications; this software model must not silently absorb those branches.
SPDX 2.2.1 remains the ISO/IEC 5962:2021 text while operational SBOM practice has moved to SPDX 3.x and CycloneDX 1.7.
A withdrawn package version in an ecosystem registry is not always the same event as CSAF document status withdrawn or CoSWID software removal.
regional_assumptions: CISA 2026 minimum elements and NIST SWID guidance are US-origin instruments adopted with international partners; they are not global law.
CPE and NVD matching are US NIST operational practice; other jurisdictions may prefer PURL/OSV matching.
CSAF has strong European implementation (BSI co-editorship) and TLP-based distribution that may differ from US federal sharing rules.
EU CRA and BSI TR-03183 may impose stricter SBOM field and format constraints on products placed on the EU market than CISA 2026.
UNSPSC classification on CoSWID is optional and not universally used outside procurement contexts.
adversarial_checks: Component/package file-level and ecosystem-registry internals were pushed to WM-SFT-007 rather than duplicated as local findings.
License legal instruments and organization masters are references, not local objects, despite CISA Component License and CoSWID licensor roles.
CVE/CWE catalogues are not mastered; only product affectation and VEX status are local.
No conformance to SPDX, CycloneDX, CSAF, ISO 19770-2 or 12207 is claimed.
Dates and version strings were rejected as identifiers; tag-id, spdxId, PURL and master-system ids are required.
Producer catalogue versus operator inventory ownership was kept split so public projections cannot leak deployment location.
SaaS and AI extras were marked as CISA-noted gaps rather than invented fields.
Patch-versus-upgrade and corpus-versus-primary tag types were included as rare lifecycle cases with RFC 9393 primary support.
